description: Apply a floor pattern to a width×height rectangle of tiles starting at (x,y) on `level`. If fill=true the server flood-fills connected same-pattern tiles instead of a fixed rectangle. Prerequisite: you are the lot owner (handler-side; server-side BuildBuyRoommate+ via Validator.CanBuildTool). Effect: floor.Pattern at the targeted tiles flips to `pattern` — observable via query-architecture. Cost: floor material price × area, debited from lot funds. Denial silent (OQ-8). Wire: VMNetArchitectureCmd { Commands: [{ Type: FLOOR_RECT | FLOOR_FILL, level, x, y, x2=width, y2=height, pattern }] }.
call_signatures:
cf $CF paint-floor --x --y --pattern

--fill true # flood-fill connected same-pattern tiles
common_mistakes: fill=true switches to flood-fill (FLOOR_FILL); otherwise rectangle (FLOOR_RECT).
perception_hints: Am I the owner? perception.lot.owner_is_me — architecture ops are owner-only
Your position (to anchor where to build): perception.avatar.position.x, .y (tile coords — arch ops accept tile coords directly, unlike walk-to)
Walls/floors are NOT exposed in perception — use query-architecture (test helper) if you need pre/post state
refuse_conditions: caller is not lot owner → returns ok:false with 'caller is not lot owner (owner_id=..., me=...)'
required tile coords (x, y) missing → returns ok:false with '<verb> requires x, y ...'
width/height/length <= 0 where specified → returns ok:false with specific bounds error
